nehemiah.13.p1.b1.text: At that time the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and in it they found the passage stating that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God …

nehemiah.13.p1.b2.text: because … had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).

nehemiah.13.p1.b3.text: As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent.

nehemiah.13.p2.b1.text: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God and had prepared for Tobiah a large room …

nehemiah.13.p2.b2.text: While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, because I had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his reign.

nehemiah.13.p2.b3.text: … Some time later I obtained leave from the king …

nehemiah.13.p2.b4.text: to return to Jerusalem. Then I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done on behalf of Tobiah by providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.

nehemiah.13.p3.b1.text: And I was greatly displeased and threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.

nehemiah.13.p3.b2.text: Then I ordered that the rooms be purified …

nehemiah.13.p3.b3.text: … and I had the articles of the house of God restored to them, along with the grain offerings and frankincense.

nehemiah.13.p4.b1.text: I also learned that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for performing the service had gone back to their own fields.

nehemiah.13.p4.b2.text: Why has the house of God been neglected?

nehemiah.13.p4.b3.text: and all Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.

nehemiah.13.p4.b4.text: Remember me for this, O my God …

nehemiah.13.p5.b1.text: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys …

nehemiah.13.p5.b2.text: Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.

nehemiah.13.p5.b3.text: What is this evil you are doing—profaning the Sabbath day?

nehemiah.13.p5.b4.text: Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city?

nehemiah.13.p6.b1.text: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath …

nehemiah.13.p6.b2.text: … I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath.

nehemiah.13.p6.b3.text: Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem …

nehemiah.13.p6.b4.text: Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.

nehemiah.13.p6.b5.text: … Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion.

nehemiah.13.p7.b1.text: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah.

nehemiah.13.p7.b2.text: I rebuked them … pulled out their hair. Then I made them take an oath before God …

nehemiah.13.p7.b3.text: Did not King Solomon of Israel sin in matters like this? … yet foreign women drew him into sin.

nehemiah.13.p7.b4.text: Even one of the sons of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I drove him away from me.

nehemiah.13.p7.b5.text: … Remember me, O my God, with favor.
